campaigns.name: No Hallucinations, No Exceptions
campaigns.objective: awareness — put botsmith's citation guarantee in front of support leaders who have been burned by bots that invent answers
campaigns.big_idea: Every support bot promises accuracy. botsmith is the only one that makes it architectural: no citation, no answer. Run a direct-message campaign on LinkedIn targeting Heads of Support with a single concrete claim they can verify themselves in five minutes.
campaigns.hook: Your bot just made something up. Again.

sample_copy.headline: Every answer shows its source — or it doesn't ship.
sample_copy.body: Most support bots deflect nothing or confidently invent wrong answers. botsmith works differently: every reply carries a citation to the exact source passage. When retrieval confidence is low, it hands off to a human instead of guessing. Set it up from a sitemap URL in about five minutes. No training UI to babysit. Just answers your team can stand behind.
sample_copy.cta: See how it works — no signup required.

assets_needed: LinkedIn post with the hook line
Short screen-recording showing a cited answer vs. a hallucinated one
Landing page section that explains the citation guarantee in plain language
campaigns.success_metric: LinkedIn post click-through rate to the landing page
campaigns.why_on_brand: Leads with the concrete differentiator in direct second-person language, mirroring the DNA's short declaratives and trust-focused vocabulary.

campaigns.name: Show HN: Built a Bot That Refuses to Guess
campaigns.objective: awareness — reach technical founders and support engineers on Hacker News who distrust LLM hallucinations
campaigns.big_idea: Frame botsmith as an architectural answer to the hallucination problem, not a prompt-engineering trick. A Show HN post explains the confidence-gated escalation design and invites the HN community to stress-test it live.
campaigns.hook: Show HN: botsmith — a support chatbot that cites every answer or hands off to a human instead of guessing

sample_copy.headline: Show HN: botsmith — a support chatbot that cites every answer or hands off to a human instead of guessing
sample_copy.body: Built this because every bot I tried either deflected nothing or invented confident wrong answers. botsmith's guardrail layer forces every reply to carry a citation to the source passage. When retrieval confidence is low it refuses to improvise and escalates to a human. Setup is a sitemap URL — median time to first answer is five minutes. Resolves 61% of inbound chats end-to-end for Pixelhaven. Happy to answer questions about the pgvector + confidence-scoring architecture.
sample_copy.cta: Try it on your own docs.

assets_needed: Show HN post draft
Brief technical write-up on the confidence-gating mechanism
Live demo endpoint or sandbox
campaigns.success_metric: Number of comments and upvotes on the Show HN post
campaigns.why_on_brand: Concrete, direct, no hype — matches the DNA's unpretentious tone and proof-first messaging with the one named customer stat.

campaigns.name: The Hallucination Incident Thread
campaigns.objective: community — spark organic conversation in support and SaaS communities by inviting people to share bot-gone-wrong stories
campaigns.big_idea: Post an open question in r/CustomerSuccess and r/SaaS asking support leaders to share their worst chatbot hallucination story. Participate genuinely, then introduce botsmith as the architectural fix — not a pitch, a contribution.
campaigns.hook: What's the worst thing a support bot has confidently made up for one of your customers?

sample_copy.headline: What's the worst thing a support bot has confidently made up for one of your customers?
sample_copy.body: We built botsmith after watching bots invent refund policies, fake feature names, and wrong pricing — all with total confidence. Curious how common this is. Drop your story below. (We're also happy to share how we approached the problem architecturally if anyone's interested.)

campaigns.big_idea: Record a real-time screen capture of the full setup flow — paste a sitemap URL, watch the bot index the docs, ask it a question, see the citation appear — in under five minutes. Distribute as a short video on LinkedIn and as a newsletter pitch to support-focused newsletters.
campaigns.hook: We timed it. Sitemap URL to first cited answer: five minutes.

sample_copy.headline: Sitemap URL to first cited answer: five minutes.
sample_copy.body: Paste your sitemap URL. botsmith indexes your docs, helpdesk articles, and past tickets. Ask it a question. Every answer comes back with a citation to the exact source passage — or it hands off to a human. No training UI. No babysitting. Watch the full setup in real time and try it on your own docs.

campaigns.name: The Citation Audit
campaigns.objective: signups — give support leaders a self-serve way to audit their current bot's answer quality, creating a natural entry point for botsmith
campaigns.big_idea: Publish a short guide: how to run a ten-question hallucination audit on any support bot. Distribute via a newsletter pitch to support and CX newsletters. The guide ends with a direct comparison: what the audit looks like when every answer is citation-forced.
campaigns.hook: Ten questions that will tell you whether your support bot is making things up.

sample_copy.headline: Ten questions that will tell you whether your support bot is making things up.
sample_copy.body: Ask your current bot ten edge-case questions from your docs. Check whether each answer links to a source. If it can't, it's guessing. We wrote a short audit guide that walks you through the test — and shows what citation-forced answers look like by comparison. Free to use on any bot, including ours.

assets_needed: One-page audit guide (PDF or web page)
Newsletter pitch paragraph
LinkedIn post with the hook line and link to the guide
campaigns.success_metric: Guide downloads or page visits attributed to newsletter and LinkedIn
campaigns.why_on_brand: Generous and educational first, promotional second — mirrors the DNA's encouraging, unpretentious register and leads with concrete utility rather than a sales pitch.

confidence.notes: Campaigns use botsmith's own proof points (61% deflection from Pixelhaven, 100% cited answers, 5-min setup) as permitted by APP_PROFILE.proof_points. Tally DNA voice is applied as the tonal model but botsmith's own vocabulary (citations, escalation, confidence-gating, guardrail) is used where appropriate since the product is different. No numeric claims were invented beyond those in APP_PROFILE.proof_points.
